subject: maths
title: Trig Foundations — Label & Choose
welcome_lead: Today you'll learn how to label a right-angled triangle and choose the right trig ratio for any problem.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Trigonometry foundations — hypotenuse/opposite/adjacent, SOH-CAH-TOA, choosing the right ratio.
final_note: You can now spot H/O/A, recall SOH-CAH-TOA and pick the ratio that matches what's known and unknown.

concepts.def: Longest side, opposite the right angle.
The side directly across from the chosen angle θ.
Side next to angle θ; not the hypotenuse.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In every right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side and it's always opposite the 90° angle.

It never touches the right angle directly. Once you've found the hypotenuse, the other two sides are 'short sides'.

Pick the angle the question asks about — call it θ.

• Opposite is the side that does NOT touch θ.
• Adjacent is the short side that DOES touch θ.

Switch which angle you call θ and O ↔ A swap. The hypotenuse stays the same.

Decision rule — look at which 2 sides are involved (one known, one unknown):

• H and O → use SOH (sin)
• H and A → use CAH (cos)
• O and A → use TOA (tan)

Example: angle = 40°, hypotenuse = 12 cm, find the opposite side. Sides involved are O and H → use SOH. Then O = 12 × sin 40°.

mcqs.q: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the side that is:
You know the adjacent side and the hypotenuse, and want the angle. Which ratio do you use?

numericals.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 6, 8 and 10. Which side is the hypotenuse?
numericals.hint: Hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle.

free_texts.q: In a right-angled triangle, the side directly across from the chosen angle θ is called the ____ side. One word.
free_texts.hint: Think 'across from'. The O in SOH and TOA.
